findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the plan body, state the mechanism by which an `LLM-Review` vote attaches to the reviewed tree — which tree/commit hash is recorded on the vote, where it is compared at consumption, and how a vote against a since-changed tree is rejected — so the 'provably attaches' guarantee is verifiable and free of a branch-tip TOCTOU.
evidence: The AC is phrased as an outcome ('provably attaches') with no accompanying data-flow in the plan body.
All mechanism detail is delegated to `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md` ('Full audit record'), which is ABSENT from the reviewed material; `tools.md` covers only the comment-triage shard.
ABSENCE: no statement of which SHA/tree-hash the vote records, nor where it is compared, appears in the plan text.
findings.finding: The correctness-load-bearing AC 'An LLM-Review vote provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed' asserts a guarantee ('provably attaches') but states no mechanism in the plan body: which tree/commit hash the vote binds to, where that binding is checked at consumption, and how a vote cast against a since-changed tree is rejected. Mechanism-correctness cannot be judged, and the latent staleness/TOCTOU failure mode (binding to a mutable branch tip rather than the reviewed tree hash) is unaddressed in the reviewed text.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'An `LLM-Review` vote provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed'
scenarios: Implementer binds the vote to a branch tip; a later commit silently makes the existing vote 'apply' to a tree it never reviewed — the exact staleness the AC exists to close.
Reviewer cannot confirm the 'provably' guarantee is actually delivered by the chosen mechanism.

findings.finding: The AC 'No library read path can terminate its host process' names an outcome but no mechanism: it does not say HOW termination is prevented (e.g. replacing `sys.exit`/`os._exit`/`SystemExit` with raised library exceptions at a named boundary), which read paths are in scope, or how the guarantee is kept from regressing. Mechanism-correctness and completeness (did they find every exit path?) cannot be judged from the plan text.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'No library read path can terminate its host process'
scenarios: A read path that raises `SystemExit` deep in a helper is missed because the plan never enumerates the surface, leaving a library/MCP caller still killable.
Reviewer cannot confirm the change is complete (every read path covered) from the plan.
